questions.q: What is the staging layer's one job, according to this lesson?
options: Turn raw, source-shaped data into clean, renamed, correctly-typed atomic building blocks — nothing more
Join every source table together into one wide table
Aggregate raw data into daily summary tables
Generate the final BI-facing dashboards directly
questions.explain: Staging models are narrow on purpose — rename, cast, and lightly compute, so downstream models get a clean, trustworthy building block.

questions.q: Which of these is a staging model ALLOWED to do?
options: Type casting, such as converting a string timestamp to a real timestamp
Joining two source tables together
Aggregating rows with a GROUP BY
Materializing itself as a wide, denormalized fact table
questions.explain: Renaming, type casting, basic computations, and categorizing are the four things a staging model is allowed to do.

questions.q: Why are joins explicitly disallowed inside a staging model?
options: They create duplicated computation and confuse which model owns a given row downstream
dbt does not support the JOIN keyword in staging models
Joins are only allowed in the marts layer for licensing reasons
Joins make a staging model run faster, which is against the style guide
questions.explain: Joining inside staging duplicates logic across every downstream model that needs it, and muddies which model is the source of truth for a row.

questions.q: What does the '1-to-1 relationship with sources' rule mean for staging models?
options: Each raw source table gets exactly one staging model, and that model is its sole entry point into the project
Each staging model must reference exactly one column
A staging model can only be queried by exactly one downstream model
Staging models must have exactly one row per customer
questions.explain: A source table's only entry point into the rest of the project is its one corresponding staging model — never referenced raw again after that.

questions.q: How are staging models typically materialized, and why?
options: As views, so downstream models always get fresh data without wasting warehouse storage
As incremental tables, to save on compute costs
As snapshots, to track slowly changing dimensions
They are not materialized at all — they exist only in documentation
questions.explain: Views keep staging models cheap to store and always current, since nothing is cached at this layer.
